hints: Count the carbons first. Chloroethane has two carbons but propanoate has three, so Q must add one extra carbon.
Q gives a carboxylate salt on boiling with aqueous NaOH, so work out which functional group hydrolyses this way.
Think about how to swap Cl for a carbon-containing group on a halogenoalkane, and why the solvent matters for substitution versus addition.
walkthrough:
**Count carbons and identify Q**

Look at the chain length. Chloroethane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ with 2 carbons, sodium propanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$ with 3 carbons.

So Q must already have 3 carbons. Since boiling aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ hydrolyses Q to a carboxylate, Q must be a nitrile, propanenitrile:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{NaOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa} + \text{NH}_3$$

**Recall how to make a nitrile from a halogenoalkane**

This is nucleophilic substitution of $\text{Cl}$ by $\text{CN}^-$. The cyanide ion adds one carbon and forms the C-C bond:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{Cl}^-$$

**Choose the correct cyanide reagent and conditions**

For halogenoalkanes we need a good source of $\text{CN}^-$ as a nucleophile in a solvent that favours substitution. That is $\text{KCN}$ (or $\text{NaCN}$) in ethanol, heated under reflux.

This gives Q as propanenitrile, which then hydrolyses to sodium propanoate as required.

options.A: Concentrated ammonia gives nucleophilic substitution to an amine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$. This adds no carbon and cannot hydrolyse to propanoate, so the chain would stay at 2 carbons.
options.B: Dilute sulfuric acid is not a nucleophilic cyanide source. With a halogenoalkane it would at most favour formation of an alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, which has only 2 carbons and will not hydrolyse to propanoate.
options.C: Hydrogen cyanide in water is used for nucleophilic addition to carbonyl compounds (aldehydes and ketones) to make hydroxynitriles. Chloroethane has no C=O bond, so this reagent will not perform substitution to make propanenitrile.
options.D: Potassium cyanide in ethanol provides $\text{CN}^-$ for nucleophilic substitution: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ becomes $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ (Q). Ethanolic conditions favour substitution over hydrolysis, and the nitrile then hydrolyses in boiling aqueous NaOH to sodium propanoate. This correctly extends the chain from 2 to 3 carbons.
